description:
What would it be like to eat a meal prepared by the best chef in China? Today we find out, as legendary Chef Tam Kwok-Fung, winner of this year’s “Chef of the Year” in the Black Pearl Restaurant Guide, treats us to an epic meal, in a restaurant that only just opened!

Thanks to the Macao Government Tourism Office for sponsoring this episode - we would never have got this incredible opportunity without them.

If you want to be wowed by Chef Tam's cooking like we were:

comments.text: I think one important thing to know about Chinese and East Asian cuisine in general is that texture is far more important than in European and American cuisine. Asian people see texture as important as flavour. That’s why there are famous popular foods like mochi, bubble tea, and tteokbokki. Even though those ingredients in themselves have no flavour, they add TEXTURE. That’s also why some Asian foods might seem weird or scary, like fish bone marrow or chicken feet, but it’s because it’s impossible to achieve the same variety of texture just by eating plain old animal meat. Western cuisine focuses heavily on flavour but comparatively deprioritizes texture

I just realized that I was pretty spoiled when I was growing up, eating all those foods and taking it all for granted. The only thing I haven’t had is that fish marrow. But I love abalone and sea cucumber. We did have crab more often than we probably deserved. We used to have bird’s nest soup often, and it didn’t register in my kid mind what I was having, but I loved it (same with shark fin when we had family banquets). Certainly we had char siu and roast duck so often that I did sometimes get a bit sick of it, though that should be considered a crime. Chef Tam is amazingly talented, but funny and humble, such a great combination.

Even when Chinese food was purchased in little shops in Chinatown, they were mostly top-notch foods, and cheap! But things have gotten so expensive now. Still, the food is more affordable than other things, and the quality is exceptional at some places. It’s so nice to see the group eating and showcasing Chinese food from this region, because this food is my childhood. This experience hits very differently, and I’m glad they love it (especially Luke, his reactions are so precious).
